code:
# Forward pass of a dense layer:
#   output = activation(W @ x + b)      <- matrix multiply
#
# Backward pass:
#   gradients computed via more matmuls
#
# Convolutions: reshaped into matmul via im2col
# Transformer attention:
#   scores  = Q @ K^T                    <- matmul
#   weights = softmax(scores)
#   output  = weights @ V                <- matmul
caption: Nearly every FLOP spent training or running a neural network is a matrix multiply.

eyebrow: SIMT: one instruction, thousands of threads
code:
# A GPU warp (32 threads on NVIDIA hardware) executes
# the SAME instruction across many threads at once:
#
#   for each thread i in warp:
#       acc[i] += a[i] * b[i]
#
# CPU vector extensions (AVX-512) do this with 8-16 lanes.
# A GPU does it with thousands of lanes simultaneously.
caption: SIMT is why thousands of 'simple' cores outperform a few 'powerful' ones on matmul.

code:
# Tensor Cores (since NVIDIA Volta) perform a small
# matrix multiply-accumulate in a single operation:
#
#   D = A x B + C   (e.g. 4x4 blocks, FP16/BF16 input)
#
# Mixed precision: compute in FP16/BF16, accumulate in FP32
# -> more throughput per clock, without more CUDA cores
caption: This is why Azure NC-series and AWS P-series GPUs post huge gains over raw CUDA core math.
